statement: How many permutations $\sigma$ of $\{1, 2, \ldots, 8\}$ satisfy both $\sigma(i) \ne i$ and $\sigma(\sigma(i)) \ne i$ for every $i$?

choices.misconception: I started from the 14833 derangements and subtracted 28 times 265 for a chosen swap, but never added back the permutations with two or more swaps.
I counted the splits into two 4-cycles as C(8, 4) times 3! times 3! without halving, so each split was counted twice.
I counted each 3-cycle as 3! arrangements instead of 2!, so the 5 + 3 case became 56 times 6 times 24.
I only used the condition sigma(i) is not i and counted the derangements of 8 elements.

hints: Think about the cycle structure of $\sigma$.
The two conditions say that $\sigma$ has no cycle of length 1 and no cycle of length 2. List the ways to split 8 into cycle lengths that are all at least 3.
The splits are $8$, $5 + 3$ and $4 + 4$. A single cycle through $m$ chosen elements can be formed in $(m-1)!$ ways.

solutions.reliable: $\sigma(i) = i$ means $i$ is in a 1-cycle, and $\sigma(\sigma(i)) = i$ with $\sigma(i) \ne i$ means $i$ is in a 2-cycle. So we count permutations whose cycles all have length at least 3. The cycle types are: one 8-cycle, $7! = 5040$; a 5-cycle and a 3-cycle, $\binom{8}{3} \cdot 2! \cdot 4! = 56 \cdot 48 = 2688$; two 4-cycles, $\frac12\binom{8}{4} \cdot 3! \cdot 3! = 35 \cdot 36 = 1260$ (halved because the two 4-cycles are interchangeable). Total $5040 + 2688 + 1260 = 8988$. Check by inclusion-exclusion over swaps, using the derangement numbers $D_8 = 14833$, $D_6 = 265$, $D_4 = 9$, $D_2 = 1$, $D_0 = 1$: $14833 - 28 \cdot 265 + 70 \cdot 3 \cdot 9 - 28 \cdot 15 \cdot 1 + 105 = 8988$. Transferable idea: conditions on $\sigma$, $\sigma^2$, ... are conditions on cycle lengths.
